title: Bible Verses for Money Worry, and How to Pray Them | Prayed
headline: Bible verses for money worry, for the week the numbers do not work
dek: Seventeen verses for the month that does not reach, the night you cannot stop running the sums, and what to do with what you do have. With a short prayer to write for each.
desc: Seventeen Bible verses about money and provision from the World English Bible, grouped for the month that does not reach, the worry that will not switch off, and what to do with what you have. With a short prayer to write for each group.
card: Seventeen verses for the month that does not reach, the night you cannot stop running the sums, and what to do with what you do have.
about: Bible verses for money worry and provision
intro: Money worry has a particular texture. It is not one large fear but a running total, updated every time you open an app, and it follows you into rooms where nothing about it can be done. The rent, the repair you keep putting off, the month with five Fridays in it. You can be fine on paper and still do the arithmetic four times before lunch, and you can be genuinely short and find that nobody around you knows, because this is the worry people keep quietest.

The verses below are quoted word for word from the World English Bible and grouped by three versions of the problem rather than by book: the month that does not reach, the worry that keeps running once the month is covered, and what to do with what you have. Read what they say rather than what you expect them to say. Most talk about food and clothing, several narrow the promise to need rather than plenty, and two of the better known ones are addressed to people who had stopped giving anything away.

None of this is financial advice, and prayer is not a substitute for the dull practical help that moves a number: a debt adviser, a benefits check, a call to the lender before the letter arrives. If the money has got heavy enough that you are not sleeping or not wanting to be here, say that to a doctor or a crisis line as well as to God. Read the group that matches your week and leave the other two.

sections.h2: When the month does not reach
paras: This is the plainest version and the one scripture handles most directly. There is a sum, a date, and not enough between them. Prayer at this point stops being a practice and turns into a request with a deadline on it, which feels undignified, and is in fact the exact kind of asking these verses keep describing.
Notice how low they aim. Food, bread, not lacking. None of them promises margin or a cushion, and one is testimony rather than a guarantee.

verses.note: The eyes of all puts you in a queue that includes every living thing. In due season concedes a season, and does not say which week of it you are in.
Need, not want, and the distinction does real work in a verse people quote while hoping for the other one. According to his riches describes the supply, not the size of what arrives.
The young lions lack. The best equipped hunter in the landscape goes hungry sometimes, and the promise here is attached to seeking rather than to capability.
An old man reporting what he has seen across a long life, not a term in a contract. He puts it carefully: he has not seen it.
No warehouse or barn is the detail to sit with if the worry is about having no reserve. The argument is a comparison of value.
Food for the hungry arrives in the same sentence as justice for the oppressed, which is how the psalm understands hunger. Pray it when your shortage has somebody else's decision inside it.

sections.pray: There is a number and a date and I do not have it. I am asking plainly, because I have run out of ways to make it work. Give me what I need this month, and if it comes through a person, make me willing to say out loud that I am short.

sections.h2: When you cannot stop running the numbers
paras: A different problem, and the more common one: the bills are covered, nothing has gone wrong, and the arithmetic runs anyway. You do it in the car, at two in the morning, in the middle of a conversation with somebody who is telling you about their day. The worry has stopped tracking the money and started running on its own.

This is the stretch of Matthew the subject keeps returning to, and it is blunter than its reputation. It does not call the questions unreasonable. It names all three out loud, then puts tomorrow outside today's allowance of trouble.

verses.note: He quotes the questions rather than dismissing them, in the words people actually use. The instruction is about carrying them, not about whether they are reasonable.
Your heavenly Father feeds them is said of birds that do no storing. Aren't you of much more value is a question put to you, which means you are expected to answer it.
First is an order of priority, not a transaction, and all these things points back to the food and clothing of the sentences before it. Tomorrow is then handed its own anxiety.
Six words, and the second clause is a conclusion drawn from the first. Written by a man whose job was keeping animals alive through dry seasons.
Contentment is tied to such things as you have, which is smaller and more awkward than being given more. The reason supplied is not a sum arriving but a sentence about his not leaving.

sections.pray: Nothing has gone wrong and I am still counting. I do not want to spend another evening doing sums at the ceiling. Let today have its own trouble and no more, and keep me from loving money while I am busy being afraid of it.

sections.h2: What to do with what you do have
paras: The last group turns the question round, which is uncomfortable to read in a tight month and is where scripture spends most of its words on money. These verses are about handling rather than receiving: what you give away first, what you remember about where the earning came from, what the sufficiency is for.

The one about the storehouse is the most quoted and the most misused. It is addressed to people who had kept back what they owed, the test in it is proposed by God about himself, and nothing in it invites you to treat giving as a deposit with an expected return.

verses.note: First fruits means before you know how the rest of the harvest turns out, which is the whole of its difficulty. Substance is ordinary stuff, not a spiritual category.
Whole is the disputed word; these were people giving part. Test me now in this is an invitation God issues about himself rather than a method you can run.
Remember is the command, and what is remembered is the source of the power to earn rather than the earnings. The purpose given at the end is a covenant, not a standard of living.
Sufficiency in everything, and then the sentence keeps going: that you may abound to every good work. The supply is aimed past your own household.
The labor of your hands puts ordinary paid work inside the answer rather than outside it. Happy and well are modest words, attached to eating what you worked for.

sections.pray: Teach me to hold this loosely, which I am not naturally good at. Let me give something away first rather than last, and remind me that the ability to earn at all came from you. Make what I have sufficient, and make me willing to let some of it go somewhere useful.

closing_h2: Write down the number, and date it
closing: Money worry is hard to remember accurately, because the feeling outlives the facts. A month you survived and a month you nearly did not feel identical a year later, and the thing you feared in March is gone from memory by June while the fear itself is still in your shoulders.

Prayed keeps the record for you. Write the prayer in your own words, including the amount if that is what it is really about, and the app matches verses like the ones on this page to what you wrote, so you are not hunting for a reference on the evening the letter arrives. Each prayer comes back to you at three days, a week, a month and a year. The year mark is the useful one here: it hands you the sentence you wrote when you did not know how the month would close, with the date on it, next to what actually happened. Nothing you write leaves your phone, and writing is free.

Start tonight, with one sentence and the date: what the shortage actually is, and what you are asking for while it stands. Then do the dull practical thing tomorrow, which is usually a phone call. If it turns, you will have the record of how. If it has not turned by next year, you will know exactly how long you have carried it.
